    AI Overview
    Rep. Tony Gonzales, a Texas Republican representing the 23rd District since 2021, announced he will resign from Congress in April 2026. His decision follows mounting pressure from sexual misconduct allegations involving a former staffer and a pending House Ethics investigation. He was previously censured by the Texas GOP. 
    Key Details About Rep. Tony Gonzales 
    • Congressional Status: Announced resignation on April 13, 2026, after withdrawing from a tough reelection primary.
    • District: Represented Texas' 23rd Congressional District, which spans over 800 miles of the U.S.-Mexico border, including San Antonio, Eagle Pass, and Uvalde.
    • Committees: Served on the House Committee on Appropriations and the House Committee on Homeland Security.
    • Background: 20-year U.S. Navy veteran, retiring as a Master Chief Petty Officer. 
    Scandal and Resignation (2026) 
    • Allegations: Faced allegations of a coercive, inappropriate sexual relationship with a former senior staff aide who later died by suicide.
    • Evidence: Text messages made public showed him soliciting sexual photos from the staffer, leading to intense bipartisan calls for his resignation.
    • Investigation: Was under investigation by the House Ethics Committee and faced potential expulsion before deciding to resign.
    • Previous Controversy: Had been formally censured by the Texas Republican party in 2023 for voting in favor of bipartisan gun safety legislation.
